note: The recovered Step record's contract, machine-readable (kogaki#871).
src/review-draft.mjs READS these lists rather than restating them — this
file is the single carrier, so amending the record's shape is one edit and
never a two-copy divergence. The same arrangement src/record-schema.json
has with checks/check-proposal-contract.sh.
EVERY FIELD IS A FACT ABOUT THE PROSE, which is the whole design: a field
that could not be checked by pointing at the passage would be the reviewer
asserting rather than recovering, and the comparison downstream would have
nothing to bind to. That is why `forbidden_keys` exists — the reviewer
writes no verdicts and no advice, and a record carrying one is refused
rather than accepted-and-ignored, because an ignored field still shaped
the reading that produced the rest of the record.
`spans_lie_inside_the_step` is the second half of the same rule. A span is
a pair of DRAFT LINE NUMBERS — the coordinate the trace already uses, so a
reviewer, the Harness and a later reader all cite the same numbers — and
one pointing outside the passage is not evidence about the passage.
AN EMPTY ARRAY IS AN ANSWER AND AN ABSENT KEY IS NOT. `terms_introduced`,
`concessions` and `restates` are each legitimately empty for a passage
that introduces, concedes or repeats nothing — so they are REQUIRED and
may be `[]`. Making them optional would leave a reviewer who simply did
not look indistinguishable from one who looked and found none.

claims.why_min: a passage asserting nothing is not a Step; an empty claims list is a reviewer who did not read rather than a passage with no content
